title: feat: add Fal fallback for Z-Image
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `fal-ai/z-image/turbo` as a fallback only after the Z-Image Vast pool fails with HTTP 503 or a network error.
- Keeps the public `zimage` model, aliases, Vast provider attribution, and $0.004/image customer price unchanged.
- Adds a hidden, paid-only internal Fal route and records Fal's $0.005/MP provider cost plus fallback attribution in Tinybird.
- Reuses the existing production `FAL_KEY`; no secret changes are included.

Validation:
- Live Fal probes at 512×512 and 1024×1024; the 1024×1024 request returned a valid JPEG in 1.33s.
- 21 focused fallback tests, 81 surrounding gen tests, and 332 registry/pricing tests pass.
- Gen typecheck and Biome checks pass.

Fal API reference: https://fal.ai/docs/model-api-reference/image-generation-api/z-image-turbo

gist.headline: Z-Image grew a spare wing
gist.blurb: When the Vast Z-Image pool takes an unplanned tea break, Z-Image can now quietly take the Fal route instead. Same public model, same aliases, same $0.004 image price—less waiting around for a GPU to wake up.
gist.summary: Added fal-ai/z-image/turbo as an internal paid-only fallback when the Vast-backed zimage model returns HTTP 503 or hits a network error, while keeping the public model name, aliases, Vast attribution, and $0.004-per-image price unchanged.
gist.impact: Z-Image requests now have a second generation path during Vast pool outages, with Fal fallback usage and its $0.005-per-megapixel provider cost recorded in Tinybird.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Z-Image as a cozy image-generation greenhouse with one sleepy Vast GPU machine briefly showing a tiny 503 sign, while Polli—wearing a small mechanic tool belt—opens a warm, discreet side path to a friendly Fal-powered art printer. The visual should communicate graceful redundancy rather than failure: the same finished pixel landscape emerges from the printer, with code-plants and flowers growing around the routing cables.
